case_title: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Man Singh
accused_occupation: Buffalo Attendant in the Veterinary Department
offence_category: Forgery, Cheating/Fraud, Criminal breach of trust
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.468, s.471, s.419 and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for one year and fine of Rs.2000/-
neutral_facts: The accused was prosecuted for forging a certificate and using it to procure an appointment as a Buffalo Attendant in the Veterinary Department. The trial court convicted him for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 471, and 419 of the IPC and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for one year and a fine of Rs.2000/-. The accused filed an appeal, which was dismissed by the Appellate Court. A criminal revision was filed in the High Court, which affirmed the conviction but reduced the sentence to the period already undergone and increased the fine to Rs.10,000/-. The accused deposited the fine and then filed a petition under Section 482 CrPC seeking the benefit of the Probation of Offenders Act. The High Court granted the benefit of probation, stating that the sentence already undergone would not affect the accused's service career. The Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order, holding that the High Court had no power to alter its own order under Section 482 CrPC and that the manner in which probation was granted was not legal.
